I computed all eight answers and saved them to `/work/answer.json`. Every value except e and h was also recomputed with a separate SQL query and matched; e and h come only from the Python script.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Q3 top segment by net sales | **smb**, 320,010,543원 |
| b. Q3 customers with a paid order | **248** |
| c. Q3 top category by net sales | **acc**, 264,267,804원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | **2025-07** (327,825,296원) |
| e. Q3 customer with the largest refunds | **u146@ex.com** (1,890,000원, no tie) |
| f. Q3 customers with 2+ paid orders | **234** |
| g. Q3 average net sales per order | **703,336원** (1,259 orders) |
| h. Growth from August to September | **1.7%** (276,489,994 → 281,181,452원) |

**Choices I made where the data allowed more than one reading:**
- **Segment for shared emails (a):** 28 email addresses have accounts in different segments. I credited each order to the segment of the account that placed it. If each person instead gets the segment of their oldest account, smb still comes first but its total changes to 313,135,904원. So the segment answer holds either way, but the amount depends on this choice.
- **Refund timing:** refunds have no date of their own, so each refund is subtracted in the month and quarter of its original order. All refunds are on paid orders.
- **Fully refunded orders:** a paid order still counts as an order for b, f and g even if its net sales are zero after refunds.

STATUS: DONE
